title: Cargill Ghosted the Bootheel for Three Years

intro_meme.prompt: A cartoon grain-elevator character wearing sunglasses on a spotlighted stand-up comedy stage, arms crossed, one eyebrow raised, microphone in hand, ready to roast.

outro_meme.prompt: The same sunglasses-wearing grain-elevator character now laughing hard, doubled over, pointing off toward a glowing sign that reads 'READ MORE.'

sources.fact: Cargill announced a 62-million-bushel-a-year soybean plant near Caruthersville in May 2022, promising 45 full-time jobs paying more than double the county average.
Cargill paused the project in June 2023, citing 'shifting market dynamics,' with no updated timeline given — and none has surfaced since.

lines.text: Nate, remember Cargill promised the Bootheel a sixty-two-million-bushel soybean plant?

lines.voice_instructions: Channel Richard Pryor-style stand-up energy: exasperated, escalating, physically reactive delivery — real gasps, real disbelief, voice cracking on the big number. This is two friends losing it together over something absurd, not a news broadcast. Real cursing where the line calls for it, land every word of it like a punchline, not a warning label.
